newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil steady on French strike, arb queried.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil steady on French strike, arb queried.

text.p: NWE gas oil premiums were mildly firmer on Thursday on an intensifying refinery strike in France but traders were divided over the prospects of an arb to Asia.
"We all watch France. So far I haven't seen a big influence (of the strike), but it is generally supportive," said a trader.
Traders agreed the strike by Elf workers had removed roughly around 140,000 tonnes from the gas oil market so far but they estimated the main bullish effect would come in January.
German demand was slow, hit in part by higher screen values, but traders added Elf was not seen buying large amounts either.

Traders said a potential arb to Asia had been created by rising Singapore gas oil prices and had focused attention on an Indian Oil Corp gas oil tender expected out late on Friday. But traders differed over whether the play was yet workable.
Dec IPE futures rose $5.50 to $229.75 a tonne, helped higher by NYMEX strength and the French oil workers' strike.
Heating oil barge premiums slid in reaction to higher futures, being done at done at Dec IPE flat and +$0.25, 75 cents lower as traders unwound positions ahead of the screen expiry.
Heating oil cargoes were up $2 at Dec IPE +$6/8 for prompt. Low sulphur diesel was steady at +$17/18.
